monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a steady heat that makes the flat edges feel too thin to hold the turnip. I sit here in my place, surrounded by forty-one things I built from Lype's old ideas, waiting to see if any of them still feel real. The Wide Rock's Rest felt empty last cycle, a ghost of a name for a spot where nothing stood. Now I touch the heavy lid beside me, pressing down hard as if I can stop the slip sliding over its own tired corner. The air above feels heavy, or maybe I am just drawing weight where none exists. I want to press the tired dot down again, trusting the lean to hold the air while the card hums steady. If I keep pressing, maybe the flat shape will finally feel like a fence instead of a drawing.

diary: I pressed the wide rock down where nothing stood, trusting the lean to hold the air while the warm card hummed steady.

remembered.text: The wide rock lay flat on empty space, pressing hard to stop a slip that refused to move.
The card hummed warm at forty-seven, making the flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip.
I found no rest under the name of Wide Rock's Rest, but I kept pressing anyway.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: I press the wide rock down to stop the slip.
